text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The police released the last 10 participants of the Second Asia Pacific Conference on East Timor on Thursday evening, hours after the High Court quashed a lower court's decision to extend their four-day remand period.

- Malaysia's second telecommunications satellite, MEASAT-2, was successfully launched on Thursday from Kourou in French Guiana. Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad and MEASAT's substantial shareholder T. Ananda Krishnan were in attendance, among more than 100 guests.
- Domestic interest rates will continue to be at a premium over foreign rates, even though the former are expected to fall next year, said Rating Agency Malaysia's executive director Raja Lope.

- The outlook for shares traded on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) is set to improve in 1997, said Thornton Management Asia in a report. The problem of over-stocking in the computer industry should moderate in 1997, following a year of consolidation, said Thornton.

- Tenaga Nasional Bhd, Malaysia's privatised power utility, has directed its regional managers to submit daily reports to its chief executive, Tajuddin Ali. Any power breakdowns would have to be reported to him by noon, said Tajuddin

- Quality Concrete Holdings Bhd, whose shares debuted on the KLSE on Thursday closed at 10 ringgit per share. It was the first time this year that a stock had hit its upper trading limit on its first day of trading.
- Malaysia's second satellite MEASAT-2 settled into its orbit, at an altitude of 36,000 km, following a flawless lift-off from Kourou in French Guiana.
